note: How operators become agents. One invocation of one operator is one agent, created fresh on the operator's own profile (operator.json → resources) with the refs its operator.json declares and nothing else. The orchestrator owns dispatch: it validates the input, starts the agent, validates the output, and follows routing.json to the next operator, user, or external party. It never merges two operators into one agent and never lets an agent start another.

agent.grants: operator.json → resources.requires, and nothing the profile would otherwise permit
agent.refs: operator.json → refs, resolved through alias/alias.json; an unlisted location is unreadable
agent.isolation: fresh, no inherited turns; a critique inside an operator is a step of the same agent
agent.writes: only @dynamic/<file> in its own step folder, registered in output.artifactRefs

concurrency.rule: at most maxConcurrentAgents agents at once, and never two agents whose refs share a writable location
concurrency.sharedCheckout: two agents may read one checkout; only one may hold it for writing (backend.implement, fe.source.apply, git.publish are exclusive per checkout)
concurrency.sharedRoot: business.decide is exclusive per businesses root; platform.operate is exclusive per runtime owner

handoff.carrier: the typed receipt <receiptType>.json (and changes.md where source was written) in the step folder; the next agent reads them as @dynamic/<file>, nearest earlier producer wins
handoff.resume: a blocked receipt with a resume token re-enters the same operator as a new agent
handoff.stop: routing.json kind user or external ends automation; the orchestrator reports and waits

files.session.json: id, project, startedAt, status (running | blocked | done), steps[] in order: {n, operator, invocationId, startedAt, outcome, receipt}
files.leases/: one file per writable location this session holds (checkout, businesses root, runtime owner); the orchestrator refuses a second session that needs the same lease
files.steps/<n>.<operator.id>/: that step's @dynamic folder: <receiptType>.json always; changes.md when the step wrote source; the artifacts its Sequence names; input.project.artifactRootRef equals this path

session.read: @dynamic/<file> resolves to the nearest earlier step that wrote <file>; two writers in one session (backend.implement then fe.source.apply) therefore have two changes.md, and quality.verify after fe.source.apply reads the frontend one; @dynamic/steps/<n>/<file> pins a specific step when a consumer needs the earlier one
lifecycle: create: the orchestrator writes session.json and takes the leases before the first agent starts
step: each agent gets a fresh steps/<n>.<operator.id>/ folder and writes only there
block: a blocked receipt keeps the session on disk with status blocked so a resume re-enters the same step folder as step n+1

done: when routing reaches user or external, or the last operator emits, the orchestrator releases the leases and deletes the session folder; what survives is what the steps published (commits, business heads, UAT pairs, remote runs) and any audit record the owner copies out first
